name: fastrand (wyrand PRNG)
baseline: rand's StdRng (ChaCha12, the algorithm behind ThreadRng and rand::rng()) and rand's SmallRng
verdict_reason: A third-party criterion run on an M1 Max measured fastrand's Rng at 0.51 ns per u64 against 4.11 ns for StdRng and 1.13 ns for SmallRng, and 21.49 GB/s filling 1 KiB against 2.02 GB/s and 7.05 GB/s. A second third-party run on a Ryzen 1700 also put it ahead of SmallRng.
tier_reason: Two benchmarks by authors of other RNG crates, independent of fastrand and rand, with CPUs stated; rustc versions not stated.
claimed_speedup: One u64: 0.51 ns vs 4.11 ns for StdRng (ChaCha12) and 1.13 ns for SmallRng; fill 1 KiB: 21.49 GB/s vs 2.02 GB/s and 7.05 GB/s (Apple M1 Max). Ryzen 1700: around 820-830ps per u64 vs 1.16ns for SmallRng.
workload: Single-threaded criterion: one u64 draw, one u32 draw, filling a 1 KiB buffer; second source: unbounded u64 generation.
hardware: Apple M1 Max; AMD Ryzen 1700 at 3.7GHz
os: Windows 10 x64 for the Ryzen run; not stated for the M1 Max run
platforms: All targets; no_std without the global thread-local functions
one_liner: Small wyrand-based RNG: 0.51 ns per u64 against 4.11 ns for rand's StdRng and 1.13 ns for SmallRng on an M1 Max.
how_it_is_fast: Wyrand keeps 8 bytes of state. Each draw adds a constant to the state and scrambles it with one 64x64-to-128-bit multiply and an XOR of the two halves, with no buffering, reseeding or cipher rounds, against the ChaCha12 block function behind StdRng and ThreadRng.
use_it_when: Simulations, games, tests, shuffling and sampling where predictability does not matter
Crates that want a tiny, dependency-free RNG
skip_it_when: Keys, tokens, nonces or anything security-relevant: wyrand is not cryptographic
Code built on rand's Rng traits and distributions, which fastrand does not implement
caveats: The M1 Max run measured fastrand::Rng instances; the global fastrand:: functions add a thread-local access
Both sources are written by authors of competing wyrand crates (rapidrand, turborand)
ThreadRng itself was not measured; StdRng runs the same ChaCha12 algorithm
tradeoffs: Not cryptographically secure; state is recoverable from a few outputs

evidence.quote: Single-threaded criterion benchmarks from `rapidrand-bench` on an M1 Max.
tested on Windows 10 x64 on an AMD Ryzen 1700 clocked at 3.7Ghz with 32GB RAM at 3066Mhz.
consistently performing around 820-830ps for generating a `u64` value. `SmallRng` performs around 1.16ns
The currently selected algorithm is ChaCha (12-rounds).
